A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the public sector employees perceive the ideal psychological contract as a combination of obligations, such as job security, training, promotion and career development opportunities, which are not always fulfilled.
the employees' perception on the ideal psychological contract varies between the private and the public sector.

employees working in public sector organizations are more likely to value organizational obligations related to career development, while those working in private sector organizations are more inclined to value those related to the provision of training and development opportunities.

the psychological contract is an effective tool for managing the relationship between the employee and employer.
employees' perceptions of the desired psychological contracts differ across sectors.
